$comment:
Templates are ATTRIBUTE-shaped, never geography-shaped. Nothing here says 'country' — they ask about an entity's attribute. That is what lets a wildlife or astronomy pack reuse them unchanged in v3.0, and it is the single most important property in this file.

CLOSED GAP, recorded because the note that replaced it was wrong for longer than the bug was. tpl.location-of.mc4 built for 35 of 65 countries: its distractors were `same-region`, so the wrong answers were other SUBREGIONS of the same region — and North America, South America and Oceania hold exactly one apiece, Asia three. The consequence was the one accessibility.md forbids outright: tpl.country-to-map.mc4 built for all 65 and is what a SIGHTED user gets, so for thirty countries a screen-reader user got no location question at all while a sighted user did. The `other-values` fallback fixed it — the option space for a value-answer question is the set of VALUES, not the set of entities — and this comment went on describing it as open. packages/engines/src/content/thesis.test.ts now asserts the parity from the declared screenReaderSafe/equivalentTemplate pairing, so a future visual template inherits the check by declaring its sibling, and a regression fails rather than being written down.

SAME LESSON, SECOND ATTRIBUTE. tpl.currency.mc4's fallback was `same-region` and is now `other-values`, for the reason above and for a reason that only appeared once the currency values stopped carrying their own country's demonym (see facts.currencies.v1.json). Short names collide by design — Australia, New Zealand and Fiji all answer "dollar" — so in Oceania, where the region IS the subregion, the primary pool and the fallback pool are the same four countries and three of them read identically. Nine questions across Oceania and South America were dropped for want of a distractor while sixty usable values sat one strategy away. The option space for a value-answer question is the set of VALUES.
